title_en: Liu Tianzhen v. Sun Renfang and Li Xia — dispute over right to health
ruling_gist_en: When an individual shopkeeper who operates a daily necessities store allows others to conduct product promotion services on his/her business premises, as the premises provider, he/she shall conduct necessary examination of the legality and appropriateness of the advertised products and services. If failing to fulfill this duty, causing damage to others, he/she shall bear corresponding fault liability according to law.

full_text_en:
Liu Tianzhen v. Sun Renfang and Li Xia — dispute over right to health

Ruling Summary

When an individual shopkeeper operating daily necessities permits others to conduct product promotion services within his business premises, as the provider of the venue, he shall conduct necessary review of the legality and appropriateness of the promoted products and services. If he fails to fulfill this duty, causing harm to others, he shall bear corresponding fault liability in accordance with the law.

Plaintiff: Liu Tianzhen, female, 33 years old, Han Chinese, residing in Jiangdu District, Yangzhou City.

Defendant: Sun Renfang, female, 33 years old, Han Chinese, residing in Jiangdu District, Yangzhou City.

Defendant: Li Xia, female, 35 years old, Han Chinese, residing in Zhengzhou City, Henan Province.

The plaintiff, Liu Tianzhen, filed a lawsuit with the People's Court of Jiangdu District, Yangzhou City, Jiangsu Province, against the defendants, Sun Renfang and Li Xia, over a dispute concerning the right to health.

The plaintiff, Liu Tianzhen, alleged: On the afternoon of March 22, 2013, the plaintiff went to the physiotherapy shop operated by the defendant, Sun Renfang, for physiotherapy and beauty treatment. During this period, the plaintiff tried a Sanwushu digital meridian therapeutic apparatus and immediately felt unwell. The defendant instructed the plaintiff to drink plenty of water at home to recover, but the plaintiff's symptoms did not improve regardless of how much water she drank, and deteriorated to a critical condition. After emergency treatment at Subei People's Hospital of Jiangsu Province, she was diagnosed with water intoxication. As negotiations between the parties regarding compensation failed repeatedly, the plaintiff initiated this lawsuit to protect her lawful rights and interests, demanding that the defendants compensate her for various losses totaling RMB 100,000.

The defendant, Sun Renfang, argued: At the time, it was Ms. Li Xia, the senior manager of Rongge Company, who performed the physiotherapy on the plaintiff, Liu Tianzhen, and during the process, it was the defendant, Li Xia, who asked the plaintiff to drink plenty of water. I primarily helped dredge the plaintiff's meridians. In fact, I was only responsible for boiling water at that time and did not help the plaintiff with physiotherapy, nor did I operate physiotherapy instruments. Li Xia should be added as a defendant in this case, and no one expected this to happen. I am unable to compensate the plaintiff for her losses.

The defendant, Li Xia, did not respond or provide any evidence.

The People's Court of Jiangdu District, Yangzhou City, found at first instance:

The defendant, Sun Renfang, is an individual proprietor of Renfang Daily Necessities Business Department in Xiannu Town, Jiangdu District, a franchise store of Rongge Science and Technology Group. The defendant, Li Xia, is the sales manager of Rongge Science and Technology Group Company. The plaintiff, Liu Tianzhen, had previously purchased health products from Renfang Daily Necessities Business Department. On March 22, 2013, Li Xia brought three digital meridian therapeutic apparatuses to Renfang Daily Necessities Business Department operated by Sun Renfang for guidance. Sun Renfang then contacted Liu Tianzhen. During the guidance, Li Xia introduced to Liu Tianzhen that the digital meridian therapeutic apparatus could unblock meridians and used the apparatus on Liu Tianzhen by attaching it to the Neiguan acupoint on the wrist. During this process, Li Xia also instructed Liu Tianzhen to drink large amounts of warm boiled water. Later, Liu Tianzhen felt unwell and experienced vomiting. That afternoon, Liu Tianzhen went again to Renfang Daily Necessities Business Department, where the digital meridian therapeutic apparatus was used on her, and she continued to drink large amounts of warm boiled water. In the evening, Liu Tianzhen again felt unwell and was sent to Yangzhou Hongquan Hospital for treatment, and was later transferred to Subei People's Hospital of Jiangsu Province. Her admission diagnosis was "water intoxication; electrolyte metabolism disorder; status epilepticus." Liu Tianzhen was discharged on March 30, 2013, with post-discharge instructions: rest and outpatient follow-up. As negotiations between the plaintiff and defendants regarding compensation failed, Liu Tianzhen filed a lawsuit with the court, demanding that the two defendants compensate her for various losses, including medical expenses and lost wages, totaling RMB 100,000. During the proceedings, Liu Tianzhen clarified her claim as seeking compensation totaling RMB 39,556.12 from the two defendants.

It was also found that the aforementioned digital meridian therapeutic apparatus was not a product manufactured or sold by Rongge Science and Technology Group. The defendant Li Xia's conduct toward the plaintiff, Liu Tianzhen, was her personal act.

It was further found that on March 25, 2013, an inspection by the Food and Drug Administration of Jiangdu District, Yangzhou City, at Renfang Daily Necessities Business Department found a "Health Messenger Digital Meridian Therapeutic Apparatus." The product's outer packaging, body, and instruction manual did not indicate the manufacturer, registration certificate number, or production date. The outer packaging indicated the scope of application as: "frozen shoulder, hypertension, irregular menstruation, and various acute and chronic conditions," and also bore the words "Yue Yao Guan Xie Sheng Chan Xu 20061375" and "Medical Device Business License Yue 023415" and other markings. The Jiangsu Provincial Food and Drug Administration, based on the intended purpose, mechanism of action, and working method of the "Health Messenger Digital Meridian Therapeutic Apparatus," confirmed that this product should be managed as a Class II medical device.

The People's Court of Jiangdu District, Yangzhou City, held at first instance:

The right to health of citizens is protected by law. In this case, the defendant, Li Xia, as the guiding instructor, used an unregistered product on the plaintiff, Liu Tianzhen. During the guidance, she neither clearly informed Liu Tianzhen of the special circumstances and precautions for using the product nor provided improper guidance, such as requiring Liu Tianzhen to drink large amounts of water, leading to the incident. She should bear primary fault liability. The defendant, Sun Renfang, as the organizer and provider of the guidance venue, failed to set up distinguishing signs indicating that the digital meridian therapeutic apparatus had no connection with the products she operated, and provided auxiliary services during the process. She should also bear corresponding legal liability in accordance with the law. According to the provisions of the Tort Liability Law, the court determined Liu Tianzhen's lawful losses as follows: 1. Medical expenses. Liu Tianzhen claimed medical expenses of RMB 21,076.12, but the medical expense receipts she provided from Yangzhou Hongquan Hospital and Subei People's Hospital of Jiangsu Province totaled RMB 20,125.98. Sun Renfang raised no objection to the medical expenses. Based on the medical expense receipts for Liu Tianzhen's injury diagnosis and treatment, the court confirmed Liu Tianzhen's medical expenses as RMB 20,125.98. 2. Hospital meal subsidy. Liu Tianzhen claimed a hospital meal subsidy of RMB 160, calculated at RMB 20 per day for 8 days of hospitalization. Sun Renfang raised no objection to the hospital meal subsidy. According to relevant regulations, the court determined Liu Tianzhen's hospital meal subsidy as RMB 160. 3. Nursing expenses. Liu Tianzhen claimed nursing expenses of RMB 480, calculated at RMB 60 per day for 8 days of hospitalization. Sun Renfang raised no objection to the nursing expenses. Based on Liu Tianzhen's injury, hospitalization, and local nursing worker compensation, the court determined Liu Tianzhen's nursing expenses as RMB 480. 4. Nutritional expenses. Liu Tianzhen claimed nutritional expenses of RMB 3,640, calculated at RMB 10 per day for 8 days of hospitalization and one year after discharge, totaling 364 days. Sun Renfang raised no objection to the standard for nutritional expenses but argued that the number of days was excessive, recognizing a post-discharge nutrition period of one to two months. Considering Liu Tianzhen's need for certain nutrition, the court discretionarily determined Liu Tianzhen's nutritional expenses as RMB 10/day × (8 + 30) days = RMB 380. 5. Lost wages. Liu Tianzhen claimed lost wages of RMB 2,200 per month for 6 months, totaling RMB 13,200, but she did not provide a certificate from the medical institution that provided treatment, only a certificate from the unit she claimed to work for, Shanghai Huangxing Catering Management Co., Ltd. Sun Renfang raised no objection to the standard for lost wages but argued that the number of months was excessive. Based on Liu Tianzhen's injury and medical treatment, the court discretionarily determined Liu Tianzhen's lost wages as RMB 2,200/month × 2 months = RMB 4,400. 6. Transportation expenses. Liu Tianzhen claimed transportation expenses of RMB 1,000. The defendant argued that transportation expenses should be supported by receipts. Based on the treatment time, frequency, and distance, the court discretionarily determined transportation expenses as RMB 500. The total lawful losses of Liu Tianzhen amounted to RMB 26,045.98. Based on the degree of fault of the two defendants, it was discretionarily determined that Li Xia should bear 65% of Liu Tianzhen's above lawful losses, i.e., RMB 16,929.89, and Sun Renfang should bear 35%, i.e., RMB 9,116.09.

In summary, in accordance with Articles 6, 12, and 16 of the Tort Liability Law of the People's Republic of China, the People's Court of Jiangdu District, Yangzhou City, rendered the following judgment on April 8, 2014:

1. The defendant, Li Xia, shall compensate the plaintiff, Liu Tianzhen, for various losses totaling RMB 16,929.89 within ten days from the date this judgment takes effect; 2. The defendant, Sun Renfang, shall compensate the plaintiff, Liu Tianzhen, for various losses totaling RMB 9,116.09 within ten days from the date this judgment takes effect; 3. The plaintiff's other claims are dismissed.

Sun Renfang, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Yangzhou Intermediate People's Court, arguing: The physiotherapy instrument was not part of her own business operations, she had no fault in the incident, and she should not bear liability.

The appellee, Liu Tianzhen, responded: The first-instance judgment was correct, and requested the second-instance court to uphold the original judgment.

The appellee, Li Xia, did not submit any defense.

The Yangzhou Intermediate People's Court confirmed the facts found at first instance upon second-instance trial.

The Yangzhou Intermediate People's Court, Jiangsu Province, held at second instance:

The appellant, Sun Renfang, as an individual shopkeeper, contacted the appellee, Liu Tianzhen, to come to her shop to receive services. As the organizer and provider of the guidance venue, she had a basic duty to review the legality and appropriateness of the so-called treatment conducted by the appellee, Li Xia, in her shop. Sun Renfang not only failed to review Li Xia's instrument but also provided auxiliary services such as boiling water, indicating subjective fault. Objectively, her conduct was related to the harmful consequences suffered by Liu Tianzhen. Her argument that the physiotherapy instrument was not part of her own business operations does not affect the determination of her corresponding liability. The first-instance court's determination that Sun Renfang should bear secondary compensatory liability was sufficiently supported.

In summary, in accordance with Article 170, Paragraph 1, Item 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Yangzhou Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment on August 11, 2014:

The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.

This judgment is final.
